home.heroSub: Eighty-eight ceramic pieces from my small studio — mugs, vases, large vases, dishes, plates, large bowls and wavy bowls. Thrown and painted one at a time, so no second one exists. You choose exactly the piece you see in the photo.
home.colLead: Tap, pick your favourite thumbnails like in a photo gallery, and go straight to checkout.

mug.desc: Everyday mugs for the morning coffee — palms, lemons, shells and cacti painted in glaze.

vase.desc: Round-bellied vases for a single branch or a market bunch — stripes, palms and cacti on warm white.

bigvase.desc: Large, round-bellied vases painted by hand — cacti, shells, palms, a lobster and folk figures on warm white.

dish.desc: Small dishes for little things — shells, cacti, palms and flowers with a painted, decorative rim.

plate.desc: Large plates for serving or the wall — a donkey, shells, palms, cacti and folk eyes with a painted rim.

largebowl.desc: Large, hand-painted bowls for salads and fruit — cobalt gardens, palms, cacti and autumn leaves.

wavybowl.desc: Wavy-rimmed bowls for breakfast and snacks — cacti, palms, shells, lemons and leaves.

home.storyP1: I’m Anna. I started out as a painter and never really stopped — I just swapped canvas for clay. I treat every mug and vase as a small painting you can pick up and fill with coffee or a wildflower.
home.storyP2: I have one small studio. I throw, glaze and paint everything myself, one piece after another. That’s why the stripes are never perfectly even and no two palms ever come out the same — and that’s exactly the point.
home.storyP3: The June drop is eighty-eight pieces made this spring. When one finds its home, it leaves the shop for good.
home.craft1P: In the gallery you tap the thumbnails you like — exactly the way you select photos on your phone. Every selected piece drops into the bar at the bottom of the screen.
home.craft2P: You review your selection in the cart, choose courier shipping or studio pickup, and complete the order. Payment is handled securely by Stripe.
home.craft3P: I wrap each piece by hand and ship within 3–5 business days. Since there is only one of each, your purchase removes it from the shop — no one buys the same one.
home.ctP: Want to see a piece in person, arrange a pickup, or order something for a special occasion? Write to me — the fastest way to reach me is by email or on Instagram.

studio.lead: A small ceramics studio in Warsaw. I throw, glaze and paint everything myself, one piece after another — which is why none ever comes out the same as the last.
studio.storyP1: I’m Anna. I studied painting and never really stopped — only now, instead of a canvas, I have a mug or the belly of a vase. I treat every piece as a small painting you can pick up and fill with coffee or a wildflower.
studio.storyP2: I came to clay slowly. First one course, then a corner in someone else’s studio, and finally my own small place with a kiln, a wheel and shelves where the work dries. The studio cat is allowed everywhere except the glaze area.
studio.storyP3: I paint by hand, with one brush, no transfer and no stencil. The stripes are never perfectly even and no two palms ever come out the same — and that’s exactly the point.
studio.fact1D: One room, one wheel, one kiln. Pickup in person by prior appointment.
studio.fact2D: Two firings per piece — a bisque firing, and a second proper one after glazing.
studio.fact3D: Mugs, vases, large vases, dishes, plates, large bowls and wavy bowls. Every piece one of a kind.
studio.fact4D: I pack by hand and send by courier across all of Poland.
studio.procH: From a lump of clay to a finished piece.
studio.p1P: I pull every form on the wheel or build it by hand. Then a few days of drying and the first, bisque firing, so the clay hardens.
studio.p2P: Onto the raw, bisque-fired surface I lay the glaze and paint the pattern with a brush — palms, lemons, shells, stripes. This is where each piece finds its character.
studio.p3P: The second firing sets the colour and the glaze. I hold the finished piece up to the light, sign the base and set it aside to ship.
studio.ctaP: When a piece finds its home, it leaves the shop for good. Take a look at what’s waiting in the June drop.

shipping.lead: How I pack, how long the parcel takes, and what to do if a piece arrives damaged. Everything before you click “buy”.
shipping.s1P: I send every piece by courier across all of Poland. Shipping costs 75 zł regardless of how many pieces you order — if you buy several, they travel together in one parcel.
shipping.s1Li3: International shipping — write to me and I’ll arrange it individually
shipping.s2P: The June-drop pieces are finished and waiting on the shelf, so there’s no production time. I send the parcel within 3–5 business days of the payment clearing, and the courier usually delivers the next day.
shipping.s2Note: I pack everything myself, between firings — which is why I sometimes ship in the morning and sometimes only in the afternoon. If you need a specific date, write to me and I’ll do my best to fit it.
shipping.s3P: The ceramics travel wrapped by hand — film, cardboard and plenty of padding so nothing moves. I label the box as fragile. I try to limit plastic wherever I can, without risking the piece.
shipping.s4P: Live in Warsaw or passing through? You can collect a piece directly from the studio — then shipping is free. We arrange the pickup by email for a specific day and time; the studio isn’t open on fixed hours.
shipping.s5P: As a consumer you have the right to withdraw from the purchase within 14 days of receiving the parcel, with no reason needed. Just write to hej@annaciok.pl and I’ll send the next steps.
shipping.s5Li1: The piece should come back undamaged, ideally in its original packaging
shipping.s5Li2: The cost of return shipping is on the buyer
shipping.s5Li3: I refund within 14 days of receiving the piece back
shipping.s6P: Ceramics can be fragile, and couriers vary. If a parcel arrives broken, please photograph the contents and the packaging and send the photos to me the same day. I’ll replace the piece with another from the drop or refund the full amount including shipping — your choice.

terms.lead: The rules for buying at Anna Ciok Ceramics. Written plainly, without the legal fog — so you can actually read them.
terms.protoNote: This is a prototype — a sample set of terms for demonstration. Before launching a real shop, the text should be reviewed by a lawyer.
terms.s1P1: The Anna Ciok Ceramics online shop is run by the ceramics studio of Anna Ciok, based in Warsaw. You can contact the seller at <link>hej@annaciok.pl</link>.
terms.s1P2: The items for sale are handmade ceramic pieces. Each piece is the only copy — once sold it disappears from the offer and is not remade.
terms.s2P: You place an order by adding selected pieces to the cart and confirming the purchase. The sale contract is concluded the moment the order is confirmed and the payment clears.
terms.s2Li1: Because each piece is unique, any given piece can be sold only once
terms.s2Li2: If for reasons beyond my control I cannot fulfil an order, I inform you immediately and refund the full amount
terms.s3P: All prices are given in Polish złoty (PLN) and are gross prices. The shipping cost shown in the cart before you confirm is added to the order total. Payment would be handled by an external payment provider (e.g. Stripe).
terms.s4P: I send orders within 3–5 business days of the payment clearing. Details of costs, timing and studio pickup are described on the <link>Shipping & returns</link> page.
terms.s5P: A consumer has the right to withdraw from the purchase within 14 days of receiving the piece, without giving a reason. The statement can simply be sent by email. The returned piece should be undamaged; the buyer covers the return shipping, and the refund is made within 14 days.
terms.s6P: If a piece arrives damaged or not as described, you can file a complaint by email, attaching photos. I review it within 14 days and — depending on your choice — replace the piece or refund the full amount including shipping.
terms.s7P: Matters not covered by these terms are governed by Polish law, including the Consumer Rights Act and the Civil Code. Any changes to the terms do not affect orders placed before they take effect.

privacy.lead: What data I collect, what for, and for how long. Short, because there isn’t much data — this is a small studio, not a corporation.
privacy.protoNote: This is a prototype — a sample privacy policy for demonstration. A real shop should adapt it to the data it actually processes.
privacy.s1P: The controller of your data is the ceramics studio of Anna Ciok, based in Warsaw. For matters relating to personal data, write to <link>hej@annaciok.pl</link>.
privacy.s2Li1: Data needed to fulfil an order — name, shipping address, email
privacy.s2Li2: The content of the message you send through the contact form
privacy.s2Li3: Basic technical browser data needed for the site to work
privacy.s2P: I don’t collect data I don’t need, and I don’t sell it to anyone.
privacy.s3P: I process data solely to fulfil an order, reply to a message and meet tax obligations. The basis is performance of the contract and, for accounting, a legal obligation.
privacy.s4P: I keep order data for as long as tax regulations require. I delete form messages once the matter is settled, unless further correspondence requires keeping them.
privacy.s5P: The site uses only essential cookies and browser storage, to remember the contents of your cart. I don’t use advertising trackers.
privacy.s6P: You have the right to access your data, correct it, delete it and restrict its processing. Just write to me — I’ll reply as fast as I can.
